defaults.permitted_development: A temporary building in England is not automatically exempt just because it will be removed later. The planning answer depends on how fixed it is, how long it stays, what it is used for and whether any specific Part 4 temporary-use right actually applies. On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.

rules.height_rules: There is no universal height allowance for temporary buildings. The taller and more visually dominant the structure becomes, the harder it is to argue that it is a minor temporary feature rather than development needing permission.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. Footprint, duration, services, foundations and the overall intensity of use matter much more than a single measurement.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary effects such as access, traffic, noise, overlooking, crowding and visibility are often what push a temporary structure into a planning application or prior approval route. On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.
rules.roof_rules: A fixed or heavily engineered roof can push a proposal toward being treated as a building rather than a lightweight temporary structure. Wind loading, drainage and visual bulk all matter.
rules.materials_rules: Use reversible, low-glare materials and details that support the temporary case. Heavy cladding, permanent foundations and full utility connections make the structure harder to describe as temporary.
